Hi Matthew — thanks for the clear list. Below is a short, operational summary and I've attached a compact one-page PDF that you can share with procurement/compliance. If you want a formal DPA clause we can send a ready-to-sign addendum (link at the end).

Quick answers:

1) Region & storage tier
- By default requests and responses for the hosted API are processed in the region closest to the API endpoint you select at onboarding. For EU customers defaults are EU (Frankfurt) resources.
- Live request/response transient data is kept on encrypted, ephemeral store (in-memory and short-lived object storage) primarily used for routing and caching.

2) Erasure timeline (standard hosted offering)
- Live tenant data: removed from the serving layer within 48 hours of a verified erasure request.
- Caches / KV prefixes: purged from the runtime cache within 7 days (most cache eviction happens immediately; we mark and sweep entries over a 7-day window to avoid tail latency effects).
- Backup snapshots / long-term backups: retained up to 90 days after deletion by default (snapshots are immutable once taken; deletion requests trigger scheduled purges aligned with snapshot retention windows).

3) Proof of deletion
- We provide a deletion certificate on request. Certificate includes timestamps, operator id, and the scope (tenant id, resources affected). Typical delivery within 14 calendar days after final purge.

4) Backups & encryption
- All backups and snapshots are server-side encrypted using keys controlled by Redwood KMS; for enterprise customers we offer customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) as part of Dedicated or Private deployments.
- Maximum retention for hosted backups is configurable in negotiation, but the default is 90 days.

5) EU-only requirement
- We can pin processing and persistent storage to EU-only for a tenant via our regional routing policy paired with a contractual DPA addendum. For stricter physical isolation (no cross-tenant co-residency) we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment.

Notes & constraints
- Operational detail: some internal diagnostic logs are anonymized and retained for 30 days by default for reliability and billing; we can reduce that on request.
- Emergency purge: we offer escalation paths for accelerated snapshot purges for critical incidents; that requires a signed SLA addendum.

Matthew — quick follow-up with specifics and next steps. Apologies for the short turnaround — forwarding the requested artifacts and a proposed DPA addition.

Specifics (hosted EU tenant):
- Live deletion: we remove live tenant records from the serving layer within 48 hours of verification. We record the operator id + timestamp and include that in the deletion certificate.
- Cache purge: marked-for-deletion entries are evicted immediately from the fastest caches; background sweeps clear all residues within 7 days. We will include the runtime purge job id in the certificate.
- Snapshot retention & expedited purge: default snapshot retention = 90 days. We can offer a contractual 60-day backup retention cap for EU tenants on hosted API as a negotiated SLA addendum (requires a signed DPA addendum). For emergencies we can schedule an expedited snapshot purge with an RTO of up to 14 days from request receipt (escalation addendum required).
- Evidence format: deletion certificate will list affected tenant id(s), live deletion timestamp, cache purge job id(s), and snapshot IDs with scheduled purge dates or completed purge timestamps. For completed purges we can include the SHA256 digest of the snapshot manifest (where available) and the operator sign-off.

Next steps I will take now:
- Send over a DPA addendum template and a deletion certificate template (attached).
- If you want the 60-day backup cap in the contract, we can mark that as an optional SLA item and route it to procurement/legal.
- If you need an emergency purge, please reply with the tenant id and the reason and we'll open a Priority Erasure request (we treat these as a managed ops job).
